title: fix(ci): clear MCP audit and service-worker test blockers
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The production dependency audit blocks main and PR CI on [GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h). The required MCP update also changes registration ordering: a failed background refresh can overwrite the original client registration before OpenClaw refuses interactive authorization. This PR fixes that regression and a service-worker test gate that could deadlock after release.

This unblocks the dependent repairs in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165334 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166224.

## User Impact

OpenClaw uses the patched MCP packages and retains existing OAuth credentials when an issuer changes during background refresh. The error directs the operator to explicit login, which can still register with the replacement issuer. This is not a claim of comprehensive clearance or migration of all historical credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Update SDK 1.30.1 to 1.31.0 in core, browser and QA Lab; update Control UI client/core 2.0.0 to 2.2.0; regenerate the lockfile.
- Apply the existing strict issuer eligibility rule before SDK client preparation. Share that predicate with token reads, preventing replacement registration before the noninteractive authorization guard.
- Make the service-worker install gate permanently released, drain all waiting responses, and cover concurrent and later requests.
- Match two existing cloud-reconciliation test labels to main’s current Worker wording, preserving every workflow assertion and timeout.

Patrick's dependency and browser-fixture commits are retained. The provider correction adds only its owner module and issuer tests. The published production delta is +17/-8 (net +9); the four changed test files total +135/-26 (net +109), protecting credential retention without new schema, configuration, public API or issuer normalization. No dependency override, audit waiver, hook-runtime change, timeout increase or new CI job.

The initial direct-main repair was refused by the pull-request-required ruleset, so this retains the existing PR route.

## Evidence

- **Audit:** the initial repair changed `node scripts/ci-production-audit.mjs` from two high MCP advisories to no matching high-or-higher production advisory. Earlier head `e023ee01` passed hosted security-fast.
- **Credential regression:** on an isolated Linux Testbox, the DCR case failed before the guard (original client overwritten; original tokens retained; 10 other issuer cases passed). After the guard, **63 OAuth tests across 10 files passed**, covering DCR on/off, explicit replacement registration/redirect, strict issuer matching, upgraded rows, refresh, redirects, persistence and lifecycle fencing. No token disclosure is claimed.
- **Source binding:** both corrected files were SHA-256 checked in the remote execution shell and match the committed correction. The newer `bb2fa83520c` parent changes only the separately reviewed browser fixture; OAuth and dependency inputs are unchanged.
- **Checks:** the provider correction passed all 27 scoped test-type graphs, production core types, lint, Knip and policy guards. Historical candidate `852af875` passed a full build (7m54s), production/script/test type graphs and policy guards, then failed full lint on two unchanged inherited max-lines violations; the full test phase did not run. Its failed correction evidence remains unqualified, with no gate-stamp transfer. The original author accepted [the explicit writer handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166217#issuecomment-6024828730) and prepared a fresh follow-up retaining `7cd2d55` and all contributor ancestry. Earlier dependency proof passed all 104 lock mirrors, dependency guards and five real AppBridge cases. No completed final-head CI claim.
- **Browser:** the maintainer's five-case service-worker suite passed, including concurrent/later gate requests and same-version terminal restoration. Independent review confirmed that repair; an additional Linux replay of the equivalent monotonic gate passed 5/5.
- **Hook-pressure investigation:** the original matched 1/5/20/deny sequence, unmatched mode and no-policy mode passed on Linux, 3/3. This does not explain the historical hosted 20-call failure. No runtime fix or inherited-failure attribution is claimed.
- **Review:** AutoReview through P2 found no additional working-tree defect in the provider correction. Its index-only finding was resolved by staging the exact reviewed files. The published browser-gate commit was independently reviewed as scoped-clean.

[Testbox runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37512272948). Exact-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper review remain required before landing.

## Real HTTP credential-boundary proof

Patrick supplied [the complete redacted trace and reproducible fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166217#issuecomment-6024365026), bound to the published provider blob `349aad690ee3c1695d6d3478f9ccfe82f34bdc11`. It uses an actual loopback HTTP listener, canonical guarded Undici transport, SDK 1.31.0, provider leases and an isolated SQLite store. The earlier 63-case suite used synthetic FetchLike responses; this additional proof crosses the real transport boundary.

| Scenario | Observed result with the guard |
| --- | --- |
| Expired legacy row at the original issuer | One token POST, resource HTTP 200, client/token issuer stamps persisted |
| Background replacement issuer with DCR | Zero registration/token POSTs, authorization error, exact original client and tokens retained |
| Explicit replacement registration | One registration POST, replacement client persisted, authorization REDIRECT, zero token POSTs |

Removing only the new client-information guard reproduced one registration POST and the stored client overwrite; restoring it passed the identical case. Before: 1 failed; after: 1 passed. Discovery state may update. The positive control proves registration and redirect, not completed interactive login. No live account or external-provider behavior is claimed.

The SDK issuer assertion is now published in `7cd2d55f1721a0e7e6edc97f16e5b87df9d7d8d0`; its exact correction passed all 42 Gateway OAuth tests. The existing author commits and the later maintainer commit are preserved.


## Final author follow-up

The only new authored repair changes the cloud-reconciliation fixture’s two stale labels to the current Worker wording. [Before/after proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166217#issuecomment-6023517033) reproduces the original 30-second locator failure and passes the full workflow after those replacements. The same failure remained in the `7cd2d55` CI retry; no retry is claimed as a fix.

With captured main `660556970ac3` incorporated, both browser files pass **6/6 in 64.55s**. The cloud fixture’s scoped `check:changed` passes, including its UI test type graph, lint, formatting, i18n, dead-export and policy checks. Fresh independent review confirms the ten-file main-relative delta is limited to the dependency update, exact previously reviewed provider/issuer/CIMD/service-worker bytes, and the two-label correction. The loopback proof’s provider blob is unchanged.

Known inherited local lint failures remain disclosed: `ui/src/components/session-organizer-operations.runtime.ts` (734/700) and `src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.ts` (703/700). Both match the incorporated/current main sources. This follow-up does not waive required CI or claim completed full native gates; fresh exact-head review and ordinary GitHub landing gates remain required.

The refreshed full changed check on the dependent integration (same MCP sources/dependencies and main `660556`) passed all production/test types, lock mirrors, guards, SDK checks and unused-export scans; full core lint also found `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-maintenance.ts` at 710/700 lines. Its blob `2d9bd4b754715b2455c37be8abd87386d0043d74` is identical on main and both candidate heads. This additional inherited violation is disclosed, not repaired or waived.
